zh: 每次搜索都从固定的鸟巢出发，而不是从上一根木棒的位置出发；被取走的位置变成 0，其余木棒的位置不变。
因此每一侧的采集顺序就是该侧木棒由近到远的顺序：先分别列出右侧和左侧的非零位置，再按右、左、右、左交替依次取，不能按长度或全局距离排序。
左列表从 bird−1 递减到 0、右列表从 bird+1 递增到 n−1，只收非零位置；第 t 次采集（t 从 0 开始）在 t 为偶数时取右列表、为奇数时取左列表，取该列表的第 ⌊t/2⌋ 项，记录下标并累加长度；总和达到或超过 100（包括恰好 100）立即停止，按顺序输出下标。
en: Every search starts from the fixed nest, not from where the previous stick was; a taken position becomes 0, and all other sticks stay where they are.

So the collection order on each side is simply that side's sticks from nearest to farthest: list the non-zero positions on the right and on the left, then take from right, left, right, left in turn; do not sort by length or by overall distance.

Build the left list from bird−1 down to 0 and the right list from bird+1 up to n−1, keeping only non-zero positions; on collection t (counting from 0) use the right list when t is even and the left list when t is odd, take its item number floor(t/2), record the index, and add its length; stop as soon as the total reaches or exceeds 100 (exactly 100 included), and print the indices in order.

explanationEn:
## Original Koddi Rules, Ranges from the Same Problem, and the Missing-Item Fix

In the fixed commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc, OA LIST/Koddi_OA/002_image.txt states explicitly that after taking each stick the bird returns to the original bird position, searches alternately starting from the right, and stops immediately once the total is at least 100; it also explicitly guarantees forest[bird]=0, a total length of at least 100, and that the needed side still has a stick in every round before the process ends. The old blocked reason, "behavior when sticks run out is unspecified", does not hold: the original guarantee rules out this case, so there is no need to invent out-of-bounds handling.

The example array in 002 is missing a 0: it has only 10 items yet outputs index 10. 003 itself repeats the complete 11-item array [25,0,50,0,0,0,0,15,0,0,45] and states step by step the lengths 15, 50, 45 at positions 7, 2, 10, with running totals 15, 65, 110, so Koddi003 alone uniquely corrects the missing item without guessing the input from another company. The original output [7,2,10] is unchanged.

The numeric constraints page for Koddi002/003 was not preserved. The ranges are explicitly taken from the same problem in OA LIST/Visa_OA/007_QQ_1741880100789.txt: 3≤n≤1000, 0≤forest[i]≤50, 0≤bird<n. The two are the same problem not just by title: Koddi002 and Visa004 match sentence by sentence in process and guarantees; Koddi003 and Visa005/006 match item by item in the complete 11-item input, bird=4, the output [7,2,10], and the 15/65/110 trace. This site discloses that the ranges come from the same problem at another company and does not claim that KoddiOCR itself gives numeric upper bounds.

The Koddi summary page's example [50,0,0,40,0,30,0,20] with bird=1 is valid, and its output [3,0,5] is correct; the correction for the invalid example on the Visa summary page is not applied here. The first public example of this problem keeps the original KoddiOCR example, and the other two are added by this site. The input is n bird plus the array, and the output is the index sequence. Upstream code was not executed.

## Approach

List the indices of all sticks to the left of the nest in decreasing index order, and the sticks to the right in increasing index order. Each list is then the collection order from the nest outward, nearest first. Alternately take the next item from the right list and the left list, add its length to the total, and stop once the total reaches 100. Even if two sticks have the same length, they are collected by position; do not sort by length or by global distance.

## Proof of correctness

The bird always returns to the fixed nest. Consider either side: sticks already taken become empty, while the other sticks keep their original positions. So the next time the bird heads to that side, what it finds is exactly the first stick not yet taken in that side's nearest-to-farthest list. By induction, the left and right lists accurately represent the collection order on each side.

The source rule starts on the right and switches direction after each collection. The reference program alternates between the right and left lists by the parity of the answer length, and reads the next index according to how many times that side has been visited, so the stick chosen at each step is the same as in the original process. The running total is also identical step by step, and controlling the loop with total<100 makes the stopping moment identical. The original problem guarantees that the needed side has a stick whenever the threshold has not yet been reached, so every read is valid. The output index sequence is therefore exactly correct.

## Complexity and edge cases

Building the two index lists takes O(n), and each stick is taken at most once, so the total time is O(n) and the space is O(n). Every positive length is at least 1, so at most 100 sticks are taken; before stopping the total is ≤99 and the last stick is ≤50, so the final total is ≤149. Both exactly 100 and exceeding 100 must end immediately. When n=3, a valid array must have 50 on each side of the empty nest; n=1000, sparse sides, long runs of 0, and sticks all of length 1 are handled directly.

## Independent verification

163 unique oracles each walk cell by cell from the fixed bird position, take the first non-zero value they meet by setting it to 0, then return to the origin and reverse direction; they do not build left and right lists and do not call the reference program. All oracle and official inputs are checked against the complete source ranges and the per-round stick guarantee. In addition, every empty-nest position for n=3..7 with values in 0/25/50 was enumerated: 2590 valid inputs were compared against the reference one by one, and 3412 inputs whose total is large enough but that lack a stick in some round were independently identified and excluded; only statistics and digests were recorded, and these inputs are not used for judging.

The official cases cover the original example, exact100 and overshoot, 100 consecutive sticks of length 1, sparse sides, n1000, the maximum value 50, extreme valid nest positions, and layouts where distance and length point in opposite directions. Two kinds of wrong programs, one with a wrong position offset after collecting (stepping once in the old direction before searching in reverse, which may wrongly take the next stick on the same side) and one that keeps going after reaching exactly 100, are each recorded as killed wrong solutions only after exiting normally on all official data. Searching cell by cell in reverse starting only from the previous stick can itself be equivalent to returning to the nest, so such an equivalent implementation must not be miscounted as a negative control.
